core_question: Where should we invest in AI healthcare solutions to achieve the highest ROI by 2026?
central_thesis: The storyline should be led by the strongest public evidence, then translated into management choices.
narrative_focus: Evidence is densest around: source quality, timing, commercial proof
structure_logic: Open with the executive decision, show source-backed data exhibits, then move through business implications, risks and action gates.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: By 2026, AI-powered diagnostic imaging will be the largest segment by revenue, driven by FDA clearances and reimbursement expansion.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Determines where to allocate R&D and sales resources.
needed_evidence: Revenue growth rates of top AI imaging companies, number of FDA clearances per year, reimbursement codes added.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: AI-driven drug discovery will reduce average development time by 30% by 2026, but will not yet significantly impact blockbuster drug revenues.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Informs investment in drug discovery AI vs. clinical-stage AI.
needed_evidence: Time savings reported by pharma companies using AI, number of AI-discovered drugs in Phase III, revenue from AI-discovered drugs.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Virtual nursing assistants and AI triage will reduce hospital readmission rates by 15% by 2026, but adoption will be limited to large hospital systems.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Target market for patient engagement AI solutions.
needed_evidence: Readmission rate reductions from pilot studies, adoption rates by hospital size, cost savings per bed.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: By 2026, over 50% of US hospitals will have deployed at least one AI-powered clinical decision support system, but physician burnout will remain a barrier.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Indicates market saturation and need for workflow integration.
needed_evidence: Survey data on CDS adoption, physician satisfaction scores, EHR integration rates.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: China will surpass the US in AI healthcare patent filings by 2026, but US will lead in clinical validation and commercial revenue.
needed_evidence: Patent filing counts by country, clinical trial registrations, revenue by region.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: AI-powered remote patient monitoring will reduce chronic disease management costs by 20% by 2026, driven by value-based care models.
needed_evidence: Cost reduction studies, RPM adoption rates, value-based care contract growth.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: By 2026, the AI healthcare market will consolidate around 3-5 major platform players, with startups focusing on niche applications.
needed_evidence: Market share data, funding rounds, acquisition announcements.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Total AI healthcare market = Global healthcare expenditure * AI penetration rate
known_limitations: Penetration rate estimates vary widely; may overstate market if adoption is slower.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Market size = Sum over segments (Number of units * Average price per unit)
known_limitations: Requires granular data on adoption and pricing; may miss smaller segments.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Market size = Total addressable organizations * Awareness rate * Trial rate * Adoption rate * Average revenue per customer
known_limitations: Funnel rates are often proprietary; assumptions needed.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Market size = Sum of value created (cost savings + revenue uplift) * capture rate
variables: Cost savings per use case (e.g., readmission reduction)
known_limitations: Value creation is difficult to measure; capture rate is speculative.

charting_rule: Charts may use only evidence_ledger values, dates, source counts or same-unit comparable values tied to public URLs.
exhibit_narrative_rule: Every exhibit must be embedded in the section argument: prose sets up the management question before the exhibit and interprets the implication after it; never stack exhibits without prose.
